questions.prompt: Which signal does Ctrl+C send to the foreground program?
questions.explain: Ctrl+C sends `SIGINT`; its default action ends the program.

questions.prompt: Which signals can NOT be caught or ignored?
questions.explain: The system keeps `SIGKILL` and `SIGSTOP` out of reach of the program, so that a process can always be stopped or killed.

questions.prompt: Match each signal with its meaning.
pairs: kills at once, cannot be caught
a timer set by alarm expired

questions.explain: `raise` delivers the signal before it returns, so the handler writes `H` first; `puts` then prints `M`.
Each `raise` runs the handler before returning, so the counter reaches 3.
`SIG_IGN` means ignore; `SIG_DFL` restores the default action.

questions.prompt: Why should a handler be installed BEFORE `fork` when the parent will signal the child?
options: The child inherits it, so an early signal cannot kill the child before it is ready
questions.explain: If the parent signals the child before the child installed its handler, the default action (usually ending the process) happens.

questions.prompt: Which of these is safe to call inside a signal handler?
questions.explain: `write` is async-signal-safe. `printf`, `malloc` and `fopen` use shared internal state and can corrupt it if the signal interrupted them.

questions.prompt: What can a process do when it receives a signal?
options: Refuse it so that the sender gets an error
questions.explain: Those are the three options (with some signals only allowing the default). The sender never learns whether the signal was ignored.

questions.prompt: `alarm(3)` asks the system to send the signal {{0}} to the process in three seconds.
questions.explain: If nothing handles it, `SIGALRM` ends the process.

options: Sends nothing, but tells whether the process exists
questions.explain: Signal 0 is only a check of existence (and permission).

questions.prompt: Why is `while (!flag) pause();` not completely safe?
options: If the signal arrives between the test and `pause`, the process sleeps forever
`flag` cannot be changed by a handler
questions.explain: The wakeup can be lost in that tiny window. Robust code uses `sigsuspend`, or a loop with `sleep`.

questions.prompt: Several children end at the same moment and the parent gets a single SIGCHLD. What should its handler do?
options: Loop on `waitpid(-1, NULL, WNOHANG)` until it returns 0 or -1
questions.explain: Equal signals can merge, so one call may leave other zombies behind: collect every child that has ended.
